items.title: From 50% to ~67% of All Major Blockchain Transactions | Solana Founder Anatoly Yakovenko
items.summary: Solana Founder Anatoly Yakovenko on borrowing Jeff Bezos's north star: "Kind of like Bezos always said, 'What's going to be constant in 10 years? People are going to want it cheaper and faster.' So our north star day in day out on engineering has always been how do we reduce latency, how do we increase bandwidth, how do we give developers more tools, more cryptographic primitives to continue building and improving applications. The key difference in how Solana approached this versus the modular roadmap and L2s and all this other stuff is that everything happens in a single execution environment. So not even a single operating system, but a single replicated distributed computer, a single instance of one – which makes it much easier to reason about value capture and a lot of benefits of composability and all these other things that are not possible in TradFi. We used to be 50% of all major blockchain transactions. I think with the recent capacity increases, it's like close to 67%." — Toly on @Fundstrat_Direct pod with Sean Farrell

items.title: Show HN: ChainBounty – improving the blockchain funding model
items.summary: Abstract. Token-funded bounties to incentivize competition-style participation in blockchain development projects would result in wider and better allocation of investment, and allow investors to diversify exposure across a field of potentially successful projects. Overall this would increase the rate of progress within development of the blockchain space. We propose a centralised platform for the administration of token-funded bounty driven development projects whereby experts allocate pools of invested capital according to the technical merits of development projects, and investors are rewarded with token allocation in funded projects. Draft Whitepaper: http://chainbounty.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/07/chainbount... We see this as bringing a variation of the YC model to blockchain - experts select large numbers of small projects and provide them with funding to reach the next level of development. This is in contrast to heavily funded ICOs where tiny teams of developers are given hundreds of millions of dollars. After feedback from HN readers: - Do you think this model will better incentivize development in the blockchain space? - What particular challenges do you think would be useful to run? https://twitter.com/ChainBounty/ https://www.facebook.com/ChainBounty-449553402088106/
